questions.problem:
Find the radius of curvature for the curve $r(t)$ at the point $r(0)$ if the curve and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the corresponding unit tangent vector are given by

$$
r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{2t},\,t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{2}{(2{e}^{2t}+1)^{2}}⟨{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{3t},\,2{e}^{2t},\,-2{e}^{2t}⟩\,.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the curve $r(t)$ and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the unit tangent, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{2t},\,1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨2{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${T}^{′}(0)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(0) & =\frac{2}{(2{e}^{0}+1)^{2}}⟨{e}^{0}-2{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0},\,-2{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{9}⟨-1,\,2,\,-2⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{9}=\frac{2\cdot 3}{9}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $r(0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{3}{(\frac{2}{3})}=\frac{3\cdot 3}{2}=\frac{9}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the radius of the osculating circle at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$,  given that the curve and its unit tangent $T(t)$ are given by

$$
r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,1⟩,\,T(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,0⟩\,.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the curve $r(t)$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of the osculating circle: 

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, the radius of the osculating circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{2}{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(2,2)$ where $t=2$, given that $‖{r}^{′}(2)‖=1,$ and the unit tangent vector to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}}{2},\,\frac{2-t}{2}⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(2)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(2)=⟨2,2⟩,$ since the point $P(2,2)$ is at the tip of $r(2).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(2)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(2)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2-t}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2-t}{2\sqrt{4t-{t}^{2}}},\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(2) & =⟨\frac{2-2}{2\sqrt{4(2)-{2}^{2}}},\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩=⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(2)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(2) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(2)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=2$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(2)}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩=⟨0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2)+R(2)N(2) & =⟨2,2⟩+2⟨0,-1⟩=⟨2,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(\pi ,2)$ where $t=\pi $, given that $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖=2,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2})⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(\pi )=⟨\pi ,2⟩$,  since the point $P(\pi ,2)$ is at the tip of $r(\pi ).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(\pi )$ and $‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}),-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩=\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{2}{(\frac{1}{2})}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=\pi $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\pi ) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})}⟨0,-1⟩=⟨0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi )+R(\pi )N(\pi ) & =⟨\pi ,2⟩+4⟨0,-1⟩=⟨\pi ,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{cos}^{3}⁡t,{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨-3{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,3{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}),3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨-1,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\cdot \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡t{sin}^{2}⁡t-3{cos}^{3}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-3{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-3{cos}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-3{sin}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨6(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}){(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{3},6(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}){(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})⟨-1,\,1,\,0⟩\times (\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & ={(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})}^{2}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \,-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}\,-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{8}\cdot 2\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{4}\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}=\frac{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{3}}{\,\frac{9}{4}\,}=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
